Vehicle launches are getting harder to land. Engineering data sits across PLM, requirements, E/E, and software tools, in schemas no general-purpose model has seen. Meanwhile every launch has to hit its start of production (SOP) and deliver the customer experience its price point promises.

SPREAD’s model reads each ticket in plain language and searches across the ticket history and SPREAD’s Product Twin of the vehicle. It links the ticket to the affected parts of the product and surfaces similar resolved cases, returning a median answer in 0.36 seconds. Engineers spend their time fixing issues instead of looking for context, and fewer issues reach SOP or the customer.

On ticket analysis, the model scored 79% against 44% for the best frontier model. On dataset queries it scored 81% against 52%, and on multi-hop questions that span several systems it roughly doubled the best frontier result. It also produced fully correct data mappings twice as often, which matters for connecting new data sources into the Product Twin.

SPREAD fine-tuned the model on 5,061 examples using NeMo Automodel and compressed it to NVIDIA’s NVFP4 4-bit format using Model Optimizer open library. A short quantization-aware distillation step then recovered the accuracy lost to compression. The full pipeline took 4.3 hours on

In engineering, that data lives in many systems that were never designed to talk to each other: requirements in ALM, parts and structures in PLM, software in its own repositories, manufacturing data in ERP and MES, results in test and simulation tools. An agent turned loose on that landscape without a connecting layer is guessing.

In my previous article, I categorized sales tasks by frequency and pattern, and described an approach for delegating them to AI starting from the top. This time, I will discuss how we applied that approach to our own product. I would like to organize where we drew the line for what to delegate to AI and what to leave for humans in "Spread Agent," the sales support SaaS we are building at kintsuba.

I should clarify beforehand that what I am writing here is not about the results or figures achieved by companies that have implemented it. It is about the boundaries we, as the creators, decided on at the beginning and the reasons behind them.
